record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove convergence of the Mayer expansion at low activity in the Kosterlitz-Thouless phase of the two-dimensional Coulomb gas, presumably through an effective multipole analysis.

evidence.quote: Convergence of the Mayer expansion at low activity for the KT phase of the 2D Coulomb gas. This is harder than the previous problem, and involves presumably an effective analysis of that gas in terms of multipoles.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional classical Coulomb gas: a neutral system of point particles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ carrying charges $\pm 1$, interacting via the two-dimensional Coulomb potential $V(x-y) = -\log|x-y|$ (with a short-distance regularization), at inverse temperature $\beta$ and fugacity (activity) $z > 0$. The grand-canonical partition function in a bounded region $\Lambda$ is
$$Z_\Lambda(\beta, z) = \sum_{N \geq 0} \frac{z^N}{N!} \sum_{\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_N \in \{\pm 1\}} \int_{\Lambda^N} \exp\!\Big(-\beta \sum_{i<j} \sigma_i \sigma_j V(x_i - x_j)\Big)\, dx_1\cdots dx_N,$$
restricted to neutral configurations. The Mayer (cluster) expansion is the formal power series in $z$ for $\frac{1}{|\Lambda|}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta,z)$ whose coefficients are integrals of truncated correlation functions (Ursell functions) over neutral multi-particle configurations.

In the Kosterlitz–Thouless regime $\beta > \beta_{\mathrm{KT}}$ (with $\beta_{\mathrm{KT}} = 8\pi$ in standard normalization), the gas is expected to be in a dielectric phase composed effectively of neutral multipoles. Prove that there exists $z_0 = z_0(\beta) > 0$ such that, for all $\beta$ in the Kosterlitz–Thouless phase and all activities $|z| < z_0(\beta)$, the Mayer expansion for the pressure $p(\beta, z) = \lim_{\Lambda \uparrow \mathbb{R}^2} \frac{1}{|\Lambda|}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta,z)$ converges absolutely, uniformly in the volume, presumably by means of an effective multiscale/multipole analysis of the gas.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has a long history: Fröhlich–Spencer (1981) established the existence of the KT transition via a multiscale expansion, and partial Mayer-expansion convergence results around dipole gases have been obtained (Brydges–Federbush; Dimock–Hurd; Falco). A 2025 preprint by Bauerschmidt et al. (arXiv:2509.09449) constructs a convergent cluster expansion around a hierarchical reference model in the two-component plasma, identifying the perturbative term with a convergent Mayer series around an i.i.d. dipole model with transitions accumulating at the KT point. A fully unconditional proof of Mayer expansion convergence at low activity throughout the entire KT phase, in the original (non-hierarchical) 2D Coulomb gas, does not appear to be settled.

status_evidence.title: Multipole and Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transitions in the Two-component Plasma
status_evidence.snippet: a convergent cluster expansion is constructed around a hierarchical reference model, with the perturbative term characterized as a convergent Mayer series obtained by expanding around an i.i.d. dipole model; Mayer coefficients exhibit transitions accumulating at β=4 (BKT).
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress: convergent Mayer-type series around a hierarchical/dipole reference, with transitions accumulating at the BKT point.

status_evidence.title: The Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in two-dimensional Abelian spin systems and the Coulomb gas
status_evidence.snippet: Inductive expansion of the Coulomb gas in the sine-Gordon representation expressing the gas as a convex superposition of dilute gases of neutral molecules whose activities are small if β is sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: Classical Fröhlich–Spencer multiscale result establishing KT transition but not a full Mayer expansion convergence theorem.

status_evidence.title: The Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions by the Mayer expansion: finiteness of the perturbations
status_evidence.snippet: Free energy and two-point correlation functions expressed as series in virial coefficients for large β; by comparison with dipole gas, conjectured absolute convergence for large β.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier partial/conjectural results on convergence of the Mayer expansion in the KT phase.
